# Self-review — iterate-2026-08-01-pr-review-stale-verdict

Seven-point checklist. Findings I raised against my own diff are marked
**[fixed]** where I acted on them before Stage 1.

## 1. Correctness

The ownership rule is a byte-identical port (`sha256` of the canonical LF blob
verified: `5cc9aea3…`), so its correctness is inherited rather than re-derived.
What is genuinely NEW here is the wiring, and its two failure modes are:

- **the anchor never lands** → cleanup looks for a review it did not post. Closed
  by `state_posted`, which is only meaningful because `post_pr_review_state` now
  raises. **[fixed]** — I found mid-build that this wrapper silently discarded
  its `CompletedProcess`, which had also left the pre-existing `except` around it
  dead. Without that fix the whole feature would have been a green-tested no-op.
- **`reviewed_sha` degenerates into "the head just now"** → the three-term guard
  collapses to the two terms that were the original defect. Closed by the
  ordering test, mutation-verified (P-W5.1).

## 2. Spec compliance

AC1–AC9 map to ledger rows 1–28. AC7 initially had **no** row and its
"the run says so" clause had no assertion anywhere — caught by Stage 1, now row
25 plus a new test. Spec Impact NONE is correct: `spec.md` carries no criterion
about the reviewer; the contract lives in CLAUDE.md rule 30.

## 3. Tests

402 pass. Three mutations attempted; **two caught, one NOT** — deleting the
`.strip()` in `_own_marker` failed no behavioural test. I recorded that as a
negative result and did not restate canonical's "load-bearing" claim, because I
could not reproduce it (the preceding `.rstrip()` already absorbs trailing CRLF).
The ledger's citations were also converted to the `alias::test` form the repo's
own citation guard can resolve — before that it matched none of them and passed
having verified nothing.

## 4. Security

The new surface is one **irreversible** mutating call. Reviewed specifically:
- every `gh` invocation is an argument list, never a shell string;
- `review_id` is coerced through `int()` in the selector *before* a candidate is
  admitted, so nothing attacker-shaped reaches the URL path;
- log output has one sanitising choke point, pinned on both producers;
- review **bodies** never reach the log at all — only ids and skip counts;
- the marker is matched `fullmatch` and positionally, so PR-authored text echoed
  by the model cannot manufacture ownership.

Blast radius on merge day is zero: ownership requires our marker and no review in
this repository carries one (P-W2).

## 5. Performance

Two extra `gh` reads on the passing path, a third only when there is something to
dismiss, one `PUT` per stale verdict. Nothing on the blocking path. The
"skipped when nothing to dismiss" behaviour is asserted rather than assumed.

## 6. Conventions

Every module ≤ 300 lines with no baseline exception (AC9), enforced by a new test
because nothing else in CI enforces a *new* crossing here. All files normalised to
LF — the `cp` from the monorepo had carried CRLF into every ported file (P-W6),
which git would have hidden by normalising on commit. Provenance headers state
divergence honestly; the `pr_review.py` header no longer claims byte-identity it
does not have.

## 7. Affected Boundaries

- **`gh` CLI / GitHub REST** — one new mutating endpoint, two new reads.
- **The `PR Review` required status** — unchanged by construction; the dismissal
  runs after the verdict is posted and never reaches the exit code.
- **`scripts/ci/` module boundary** — six functions changed import site; every
  displaced test moved with its assertions unchanged.
- **The repo's vendor-drift guards** — two new entries in `_NOT_HASH_PINNED`,
  paired with real pins in a new module so "not in the manifest" does not quietly
  mean "not pinned". I also discovered the guard keys on a literal marker string,
  so mentioning it in prose enrols the file; recorded in-place.

## Known-weak, stated rather than hidden

# External plan review — iterate-2026-08-01-pr-review-stale-verdict

- **Mode:** `iterate` · **Provider:** openrouter
- **openai:** `revise` (success) · **gemini:** `unavailable` (degraded —
  provider reported the reply was cut off, `finish_reason=length`)
- **Contradiction:** not comparable (only one reviewer answered)

## Findings (openai)

1. **edge-case / medium — one pre-mutation head read does not close the
   force-push race.** If the head changes between dismissals when several stale
   reviews are selected, a review whose commit becomes current again can still be
   dismissed. Suggests re-reading the head before *each* dismissal and stopping
   the loop on mismatch; concedes a narrow post-read/pre-write race is
   unavoidable because GitHub offers no conditional-dismiss API.

2. **approach / medium — "own marker" is a generic shape plus a shared login.**
   A different workflow using `github-actions[bot]` and the same marker
   convention would satisfy the candidate predicate, contrary to AC3. The nonce
   distinguishes the current *anchor* but does not prove an older *candidate's*
   nonce was minted by this reviewer, because any 32-hex token matches. Asks
   either for a producer-unique namespace, or for the namespace's exclusivity to
   be stated and tested explicitly.

3. **edge-case / low — duplicate anchors are unhandled.** Selecting one
   arbitrarily is unnecessary risk for an irreversible operation. Suggests
   requiring exactly one valid anchor and refusing otherwise.

4. **risk / low — the eventual-consistency no-op can leave a stale block with no
   visible explanation.** Asks that the best-effort report explicitly say no
   dismissal occurred because the just-posted anchor was absent from the listing.

5. **security / low — a write-capable path driven by API-returned data.** Asks
   that subprocess invocation stay argument-based, that review IDs be validated
   as numeric before building the dismissal path, that display sanitisation cover
   every untrusted value reaching logs, and that a test carry ANSI/control
   characters.

> Overall, the split between pure selection, GitHub boundary, and best-effort
> orchestration is sound and appropriately avoids a broad re-vendor. The main
> changes needed are to make the ownership claim match AC3 and to tighten and
> document the unavoidable head-movement race around irreversible dismissals.

## Responses

**The governing constraint is that these files are VENDORED.** The card is
explicit: *"DO NOT SIMPLIFY THE OWNERSHIP RULE — three review rounds narrowed it
and each guard exists for a measured reason."* The inverse holds with equal
force: **hardening it locally is also drift.** A safety rule that exists in two
implementations, differing, is worse than one that is uniformly imperfect —
canonical stays weak, this copy stops being re-vendorable, and the next
re-vendor silently reverts the local hardening without anyone noticing. So a
finding about the *rule* is answered by filing it upstream, and only *additive,
repo-local* guards are added here.

**F1 — accepted as a known residual; NOT changed here.** Upstream reasoned this
exact case and named it: *"The irreducible residual is a force-push landing
inside the dismissal loop; that is bounded by the `PR Review` status being
recorded per commit SHA."* The suggested per-dismissal re-read narrows the window
from N mutations to one but cannot close it (the reviewer says so), costs one API
call per candidate, and introduces a new partial-sweep failure mode when a
mid-loop read fails transiently. Filed as a cross-repo follow-up against
canonical rather than diverged here.

**F2 — the underlying concern is accepted, and it is answered ADDITIVELY.**
The threat requires another `Bot` under the *same login in this same repository*
emitting a whole `<!-- shipwright-pr-review:{32 hex} -->` token as the **last
line** of a review body. Reviews do not cross repositories, so the monorepo's
reviewer and this vendored […truncated]

# Stage 2 code review (code-reviewer subagent)

Round 1: REQUEST_CHANGES — 1 medium + 5 low.
  1 MEDIUM  `_wire` never patched the two gh boundaries ADR-117 added to main(), so every
            TestMainOrchestration case shelled out to a REAL `gh api repos/owner/repo/pulls/42`
            and the two passing cases ran the real cleanup — in a job advertised "Offline, no
            credentials". CONFIRMED by tripwire naming the exact argv, then FIXED two ways:
            canonical's two monkeypatches, plus a new `no_real_gh` fixture over the whole class.
  2 LOW     read_reviewed_head's emit sits outside its try. NOT FIXED, deliberately: the line is
            in the byte-pinned vendored module; local hardening is the drift the card forbids.
            Reviewer accepted the deferral and noted it fails CLOSED anyway. Filed upstream.
  3 LOW     marker-namespace guard was a non-recursive scripts/ci/*.py glob; a workflow step or
            shell helper emitting the marker would satisfy the ownership predicate unseen.
            FIXED: whole-repo via `git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard`.
  4 LOW     vendor-pin test promised "both directions", asserted one. FIXED with a closed
            `_KNOWINGLY_UNPINNED` set so a new unpinned vendored leaf fails.
  5 LOW     duplicate `import json`. FIXED.
  6 LOW     ordering vs stage 2's later staleness verdict was safe but unrecorded. FIXED (comment).

Round 2: APPROVE. Reviewer re-verified against the files, confirmed no bare `except:` or
`except BaseException` exists that could defeat the tripwire, confirmed pytest reports a
BaseException as a failure, cross-checked the reverse-direction set resolves to empty today, and
re-confirmed it could not construct an input dismissing a review this reviewer does not own.
Two advisory LOW nits raised and both fixed before commit: `git ls-files` needed `-z` (quoted
non-ASCII paths were being silently skipped — the same "guard passes by not looking" shape as the
two bugs already fixed), and the invariants module docstring now names the co-located guard.

Also validated the external code review's two mediums (empty-listing raise; the wrapper-boundary
raise) as correct and correctly placed.

# Stage 3 adversarial doubt review (doubt-reviewer subagent)

Advisory-must-address. 8 doubts: 1 high, 3 medium, 4 low. ALL addressed.

HIGH  - the ORDERING comment I added at the irreversible-write call site asserted
        "A->B->A is refused"; it is NOT (all three terms agree on A while the diff read
        was B), and the spec's own 5b(d) said the opposite. FIXED: comment rewritten to
        state fresh-not-exact, name the bounded residual, and defer to 5b(d).
MED   - `strip_display_unsafe` is the ONE function this port ADAPTED, and its alphabet was
        pinned by nothing; narrowing it to C0 left 50 of 82 codepoints dead with the suite
        green, while its own comment claimed "pinned by enumeration in the tests" (true
        upstream, false here). FIXED: canonical's sanitiser cases ported as
        test_pr_review_sanitiser.py (9 cases incl. a full 0x110000 enumeration); verified
        the narrowing now fails. Touched no pinned byte, so the vendoring posture never
        excused it - the reviewer's point, and correct.
MED   - Section 5 claimed the required status is "unchanged by construction"; only the
        exit-code channel was established. The dismissal loop and the status POST share a
        GitHub rate-limit budget. FIXED: claim narrowed to what was proven, and the
        shared-budget path named as residual 5b(f).
MED   - the offline tripwire lived in one module while a SECOND orchestration module kept
        its own hand-maintained _wire and no tripwire - the same failure reproduced in the
        same diff. FIXED: fixture moved to shared _pr_review_offline.py and applied to
        both; mutation-verified in the second module.
LOW   - P-W4's "277" was measured before later comments landed (actual 297). FIXED.
LOW   - two comments (test module + fixture docstring) still asserted the DISPROVED CRLF
        claim about `.strip()`, contradicting the corrective test nine lines below, plus a
        stale "27 ledger behaviours". FIXED, and the correction mutation-verified: dropping
        `.rstrip()` fails the CRLF test, confirming which call does the work.
LOW   - `_post_verdict` opened a NEW sink for raw `gh` stderr (live only because this diff
        made the wrapper raise) and printed it through `_redact` alone, so a newline could
        forge `::error::`. FIXED: routed through strip_display_unsafe.
LOW   - pr_review_openrouter.py carried no provenance and was invisible to both vendor
        guards. FIXED: canonical-source-repo/-commit/-paths/-version added (no hash, same
        posture as pr_review_gh.py).

Could NOT break, having tried: ownership forging (positional fullmatch, homoglyph,
full-width, CRLF, leading whitespace, planted anchor - the anchor needs the 128-bit runtime
nonce and loses on id ordering anyway); commit_id semantics across 8 orderings of
block-run/pass-run/force-push; exit-code coupling on every path; degenerate gh output; the
BaseException tripwire; P-W1 and P-W2 (both confirmed, incl. that this PR is itself Tier-3);
and the vendored selector, hand-diffed byte-identical to canonical apart from the header.

On the vendoring posture: reviewer judged it defensible for the selector's early-return gap
and the missing throttle (inside pinned bytes), and NOT defensible for the three findings
whose fix touches no pinned byte. All three of those were fixed.

findings.finding: AC7 requires an unmarked `CHANGES_REQUESTED` verdict to be left alone and for the run to say so. The selector returns immediately when this run’s anchor is not visible, or later when the reviewed/head/anchor SHA guard fails, without examining candidate reviews or recording `unmarked` skips. For example, during GitHub’s post-review/list eventual-consistency window, a PR containing an unmarked legacy block will only report “this run's own review is not visible,” not that the legacy block was deliberately left alone because it is unmarked.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the no-dismissal early-return safety behavior, but scan/count candidate `CHANGES_REQUESTED` rows for report-only skip reasons before returning, or emit an explicit message that unmarked reviews could not be attributed and were left untouched. Add tests for an unmarked candidate when the anchor is absent and when the head guard refuses cleanup.  The implementation otherwise follows the intended ownership, head-consistency, and best-effort cleanup design, with meaningful boundary and orchestration tests. It should ship with the diagnostic AC7 gap fixed first.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

# Stage 1 spec-compliance review (spec-reviewer subagent)

Round 1: REJECT — 3 blocking + 6 lower findings.
  1 HIGH   spec claimed all three gh wrappers moved verbatim; post_pr_review_state gained a
           returncode check that §4's own _post_verdict contract requires. §6 listed that very
           change as out of scope. FIXED (§3 paragraph, §4 row, §6.4 carve-out).
  2 MEDIUM pr_review_openrouter.py shipped outside the Design table, Option D, §5 and §7.4.
           FIXED (recorded as decided-mid-build, with the ~332 price that forced it).
  3 MEDIUM AC7 had no ledger row and its "the run says so" clause had NO assertion anywhere.
           FIXED: ledger row 25 + new test calls::test_an_unmarked_verdict_is_named_in_the_log.
  4 LOW    row 16 said "three" tests, two exist. FIXED, and the deeper point acted on: the repo's
           test_iterate_ledger_citations.py guard matched NONE of the bare-name citations, so it
           passed having verified nothing. All citations converted to <alias>::<test> and seven
           aliases registered. Suite 346 -> 406; the +59 ARE the citation checks.
  5-9 LOW  P-W4 line count, pr_review_gh drift-coverage disclosure, header naming only one of two
           canonical divergences, fixtures fidelity wording, CHANGELOG timing. All FIXED/accepted.

Round 2: APPROVE (verdict PASS). Reviewer independently re-verified on disk: all seven aliases
resolve to the modules defining the cited tests; the guard AST-parses the aliased module so a
wrong alias fails rather than passes; all citations resolved by hand; pr_review.py measures 277
lines with no baseline entry; spec.md carries no criterion about the reviewer so Spec Impact NONE
stands. Five residual documentation-accuracy nits raised, all swept before commit (stale §4 table
cell, stale suite count, "six files touched" wording, 340-vs-315 estimate/measurement, an AC3
citation lost in the row shuffle plus an uncited openrouter alias).

Post-sweep self-check found one more: the ledger's own format EXAMPLE matched the guard regex and
read as a 60th citation the guard then skipped. Rewritten as <alias>::<test_name>; 346+1+59=406
now closes exactly.
